items.title: Peter Appleyard interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, October 4, 2012
items.q: I traveled with him too, to Japan, and played Michael’s Pub with him for a month in New York. And we recorded in Tokyo.

ctx.x: I recorded for Maurice Jarre, who did Dr. Zhivago and all those films. I recorded for the greatest vocal writer that ever lived, Robert Farnon. I did his “Porgy & Bess.” I did, for Oscar Peterson, “The Canadiana Suite,” that was a highlight as a percussionist. I did Henry Mancini. I remember Mancini coming over to me and said, “No, I don’t want it played — I want it done like this” and he picked up the mallets. And then I did — I
recorded with Anne Murray, Gordon Lightfoot, oh gosh, I can’t remember them all. I recorded with Mel Torme — Mel Torment as Buddy Rich used to call him.
